crates/rs_cam_core/src/machine/kinematics.rs:541-549: `detect_firmware` is string matching. A new controller's firmware is never detected unless this changes, so the machine profile never selects the new dialect. Nothing relates it to the ControllerFirmware enum.

crates/rs_cam_core/src/machine/mod.rs:237-268: ControllerFirmware only has Unknown/Grbl/GrblHal. The request says 'selectable from the machine profile', but the machine profile holds no post field. A contributor who reads the request literally looks for a field that does not exist.

crates/rs_cam_viz/src/ui/export_wizard.rs:590: `state.gui.post.format == PostFormat::GrblHal` is an equality test, not a match. A new controller with options never gets a UI block. Also ui/properties/machine_panel.rs:542.

crates/rs_cam_core/src/export/gcode_validator.rs:116-137: PostInvariants has a field named `grblhal_words` and `no_canned_cycles`. They are booleans keyed on a dialect, not capabilities. The struct literal forces a value, but a contributor may set `grblhal_words: true` for a Grbl-derived controller without knowing what it enables (gcode_validator.rs:588).

crates/rs_cam_core/tests/fixtures/gcode_golden/*: the capture test only compares a golden when a file exists; a fixture that a post refuses has no golden by design (tests/gcode_phase0_capture.rs:18). A forgotten golden for the new dialect can look like a refusal. DIALECTS (tests/common/gcode_fixtures.rs:26) is the only list.

crates/rs_cam_core/src/gcode/post.rs:253-316 (unsupported_mcodes, mist_option, cutter comp): behaviour flags live in the TOML as optional fields with defaults. A wrong or missing flag is not an error; the emitter falls back to the default silently.
README.md:8, FEATURE_CATALOG.md:131 and the cli `--post` help (main.rs:116): doc and help lists that nothing checks.

crates/rs_cam_core/src/gcode/CLAUDE.md:25 states the rule 'add a PostDefinition row, not a branch in the emitter', but there is no row: the real steps are a TOML plus five code sites. The CLAUDE.md does not list them.
reuse_traps: `PostFormat::from_token` (gcode/mod.rs:1489) is the ONE resolver. `get_post_definition` (mod.rs:1617) wraps it for CLI strings. A contributor adding a CLI or MCP flag would re-write a string match; the comment at mod.rs:1476-1488 explains that this caused the W9/P-1 bug.
`PostFormat::to_token` (mod.rs:1467) and the serde `rename` on the variant must agree (UI-07). A contributor may add a different serde spelling and break project round-trips.

`PostConfig::apply_controller_options` (mod.rs:1565) is the one place that merges the machine profile's controller facts into the export overlay. Every export door (GUI, MCP, CLI) calls it. A new controller option written straight into WizardOverlay in one door would make the surfaces differ.
`ControllerFirmware::post_format` (machine/mod.rs:262) is the machine-profile-to-dialect map. A contributor might add a new `post` field to MachineProfile instead.
`PostDefinition::from_toml` plus the OnceLock accessor pattern (post.rs:454-489) already exists for all four posts. A contributor may write a runtime registry or a user-post loader instead.
`gcode_validator::validate` and `validate_export` (viz io/export.rs) take the same overlay options as the emitter (G8), so the validator and the emitter agree. app/export.rs:226 shows the branch.
ambiguity: Closest examples: the grblHAL addition (2026-10-08, FEATURE_CATALOG.md:132-133, G1..G11) versus Mach3/LinuxCNC. grblHAL is a Grbl-derived controller that also added machine-profile firmware detection, overlay options and GUI options. Mach3/LinuxCNC are plain TOML plus enum arms with no controller facts. For 'selectable from the machine profile' the grblHAL path is the only one that touches the machine profile, but it also carries grblHAL-only options that a generic controller does not need.

Where 'selectable' lives: the post dropdown in PostConfig (viz ui/properties/post.rs:17, project-level) versus ControllerFirmware on the machine profile (machine/mod.rs:237). Both exist and both set session.post.format. The request names the machine profile, but the code treats the dialect as a project choice that a `$$` import overrides.
Validator flags: copy the Grbl row (line-limited, no M6, no canned cycles) or the grblHAL row (M6, canned cycles, whole-line limit). `grblhal_words` is a boolean named for one dialect.

Per-dialect options: PostConfig fields with `Option<bool>` and an `apply_controller_options` merge (grblHAL style) versus fields inside the TOML. Both exist (post.rs:253-316 TOML flags like mist_option, and PostConfig mist_output at mod.rs:1550).

A new dialect is thus not selectable over MCP/headless unless firmware detection or a new param is added, and nothing enforces parity with the GUI dropdown (parallel surface).

Behaviour flags that gate emitter logic are TOML fields on PostDefinition (post.rs:238-266: prefer_one_file_per_setup, canned_drill_cycles, mist_option, supports_cutter_comp, unsupported_mcodes) and need to be set in the new TOML consistently with the separate PostInvariants in gcode_validator.rs; the two are not cross-checked, so they can drift silently (e.g. TOML says no M6 but invariants say supports_m6).
reuse_traps: PostFormat::from_token (crates/rs_cam_core/src/gcode/mod.rs:1488) vs get_post_definition (mod.rs:1617) vs hand-written string matches: from_token is THE resolver (doc at 1478-1487); a contributor adding a CLI or MCP param might re-write a match instead of calling it. Also post_format_or_grbl (mod.rs:1608) is the private serde fallback.

PostFormat::to_token (mod.rs:1467) vs serde rename attributes on the enum (mod.rs:1414-1431): two spellings that must agree; easy to copy the snake_case default (as Mach3 does) and get 'grbl_hal'-style drift.

PostConfig::apply_controller_options (mod.rs:1536-1555) already maps machine.controller facts into WizardOverlay; a contributor wanting machine-profile-driven behaviour might add a new reader instead of extending it. Related WizardOverlay::applied_post (gcode/wizard_overlay.rs, used in tests at 667, 798) is where per-export overrides of a PostDefinition are applied.

PostDefinition::render_* helpers (post.rs:343-440: render_preamble_with_tool, render_message_line, render_tool_change, tool_change_commands_m6) and sanitize_comment_text (post.rs:~150): easy to re-implement comment/tool-change handling in code rather than using TOML templates.

ControllerFirmware::post_format (machine/mod.rs:262) is the existing firmware->dialect mapping; ControllerSettings::merge_stated (machine/mod.rs:370) names every field in a destructure so new fields are compiler-forced there.
gcode_validator::invariants_for (export/gcode_validator.rs:153) is a second per-dialect table; PostDefinition fields in TOML overlap with it conceptually.
ambiguity: Two plausible 'where does the dialect live' patterns: (a) project-level PostConfig.format chosen via the Post dropdown / PostFormat::ALL (gcode/mod.rs:1507-1530, properties/post.rs:17), and (b) machine-profile-level ControllerSettings.firmware auto-selecting the dialect on $$ import (machine/mod.rs:248-269, session/mutation/config.rs:708). 'Selectable from the machine profile' matches (b) in spirit but (b) only supports Unknown/Grbl/GrblHal and only auto-detects; MachineProfile (machine/mod.rs:177-246) has no dialect field of its own. A contributor could instead add a new field on MachineProfile (parallel to controller) or reuse PostConfig.format.

Firmware-variant pattern vs PostFormat pattern: ControllerFirmware::Grbl has a post_format mapping but detect_firmware never returns Grbl (kinematics.rs:541, test at 2209), so it is unclear whether a new firmware should follow GrblHal (auto-detected) or Grbl (mapped but never produced).

Copy source for the TOML: grbl.toml (pause-style tool change, no cutter comp) vs grblhal.toml (M6, MSG, canned cycles) vs linuxcnc.toml/mach3.toml (4 decimals, M6, cutter comp); and for the enum serde spelling: Mach3 (plain) vs GrblHal/LinuxCnc (rename+alias).

Controller-specific options: grblHAL-gated UI/CLI/MCP options (export_wizard.rs:590, rs_cam_cli/src/run.rs:46, rs_cam_mcp/src/server.rs:258-271) vs the data-driven PostDefinition flags (post.rs:238-266); either could be copied for a new controller's special options.
